title: E12.5 in-flight migration — drain-by-default + forward-only rollback guard (migration 071)
design_note: Three ADR decisions are now code: (1) DRAIN-by-default = drainInstance() creates InstanceDrainRecord with state='draining'; no forced migration happens unless explicitly requested. (2) Forward-only rollback guard = guardRollback() is fail-CLOSED: calls the injected RollbackSafePort (which wraps T-0085's fn_check_rollback_safe + the new fn_count_live_instances_above_version), returns allowed=false on any unsafe/uncertain condition. (3) Camunda mapping = on-demand escalation = validateCamundaMapping() always sets requires_human_gate=true; validates wait-state-only + no-type-change constraints. Execution is NOT implemented here — this increment provides the gate, the types, and the enforcement seam.

rollback_guard_binds_T0085.how: RollbackSafePort.isRollbackSafe() wraps fn_check_rollback_safe(tenant_id, registry_id, target_version) from migration 070. Port is injected — pure core never imports pg. guardRollback() calls both isRollbackSafe and countLiveInstancesAboveVersion; either returning unsafe/nonzero causes fail-CLOSED block.
rollback_guard_binds_T0085.fail_closed_seam: If the port throws (DB unreachable, transport error) guardRollback() returns { allowed: false, reason: '..port error..', live_instance_count: 0 }. Default-DENY — any uncertainty = blocked.
rollback_guard_binds_T0085.fn_count_live_instances_above_version: New SQL function in migration 071 (companion to fn_check_rollback_safe): counts draining instances for a bundle, used for actionable error messages.
